title: Shipyard repo config
description: Schema for shipyard.config.json (committed, repo-level) and .shipyard/config.local.json (gitignored, personal override). The latter is sparse — only fields the user wants to override locally.

$schema.description: Optional schema reference for editor autocomplete.

version.description: Schema version. Increment on breaking changes. Additive changes within a major version don't bump this.

policy.description: always = arm auto-merge on every PR; trusted-only = arm only when originating_author_trust == trusted (default); never = never arm auto-merge.

method.description: Merge method every worker mode must pass to `gh pr merge --auto`/`gh pr merge` (default squash). This is repo policy, not worker choice — resolve this value rather than hardcoding a method (issue #989).

authors.description: GitHub author identities whose issues are dispatch-eligible without external-author gating. Accepts any GitHub login shape — plain logins (mattsears18), REST bot logins (sentry[bot]), and GraphQL app logins (app/sentry) — since the field is only a comparison key: an entry that matches nothing is a harmless no-op, so no pattern constraint is enforced (see issue #371). Overrides the user-global trusted-authors list (does not merge — repo override is authoritative).

backlog.description: Controls scripts/backlog-filter.sh classify's eligibility clauses that are properties of the ISSUE POOL itself (assignee ownership, a manual Someday park) rather than of an individual issue's body/labels. `respect_assignees` and `self_assign` default to the single-contributor-repo shape: assignees are ignored for dispatch eligibility, and /do-work never writes an assignment itself. A genuine multi-contributor repo — where 'assigned to someone else' is a meaningful 'not mine' signal — sets both to true to restore the pre-#1248 behavior.

respect_assignees.description: When true, scripts/backlog-filter.sh classify drops an issue assigned to anyone OTHER than --me (self-assigned and unassigned issues always pass regardless of this flag). When false (default), the assignee clause is skipped entirely — any open issue is dispatch-eligible no matter who (if anyone) it's assigned to. The clause only has upside on a genuine multi-contributor repo; on a single-contributor repo (the common shipyard-marketplace case) it has no correct exclusion to make; the #1194 erasure came from a shorthand version of the same clause. Does not affect the `Blocked by #N` / gate-label / trust / peer-claimed / time-gate / closed-by-healthy-pr / covered-by-open-pr clauses — those are unconditional.

self_assign.description: When true, /do-work self-assigns a candidate issue to @me before dispatching (`gh issue edit <N> --add-assignee @me`), in addition to always stamping the `shipyard` session-stamp label. When false (default), no assignment call is made — the `shipyard` label alone carries provenance and human visibility. The self-assign was originally documented as a 'soft-lock against parallel /do-work instances', but that claim only holds across different GitHub identities: a second same-identity session evaluates its own self-assigned issue as `assignee == @me` and dispatches it anyway, so no lock actually occurs for the common single-operator case. The real collision guard is the concurrent-session worktree/PID lock (see dispatch-rules.md), which is unaffected by this flag. Set true only on a genuine multi-contributor repo that wants @me-assignment as a visible claim marker independent of the lock.

someday_milestone.description: Issue #1406. When non-empty, scripts/backlog-filter.sh classify drops (verdict `drop`, reason `someday-milestone`) any open issue whose GitHub milestone title — with its leading `N · ` sequence-number prefix stripped, compared case-insensitively and trimmed — exactly equals this value. Set it to the bare human-readable name of your repo's 'parked, event-gated, no probe expressible' phase (e.g. `"Someday"` for a milestone titled `6 · Someday`) — never the whole numbered title, which drifts every time `shipyard:update-roadmap` renumbers phases. Defaults to `""` (empty string), which never matches a real milestone title, so the clause is INERT until a repo explicitly opts in — a repo that parks work in a milestone loosely (not as a deliberate 'stop re-scoping this' signal) must not silently lose that work from dispatch. Deliberately scoped under `backlog.*`, not `milestones.*`, and evaluated unconditionally of `milestones.enabled` / `milestones.prioritize_dispatch` — those two keys gate milestone-aware RANKING of the eligible bucket (issue #1241) and are themselves inert while `milestones.enabled` is false (see `commands/do-work/dont.md`'s `milestones.*` guard); this key gates ELIGIBILITY itself and must keep working on exactly the repo shape that motivated it, one with `milestones.enabled: false`. See `commands/do-work/setup/04f-completion-ledger.md`'s bucket 7.5 for the completion-ledger accounting and `commands/do-work-RATIONALE.md` for the full design writeup.

someday_recheck_days.description: Issue #1422, follow-up to #1406. The slow re-scope cadence for issues parked by `someday_milestone` — inert whenever `someday_milestone` is `""` (the parent gate's own off-by-default posture; this knob has nothing to gate without it). While non-zero, `scripts/backlog-filter.sh classify` tracks a self-clearing `<!-- do-work-someday-recheck: YYYY-MM-DD -->` BODY marker (distinct from `do-work-blocked-until` — a Someday park is not a calendar gate, only its recheck cadence is) per Someday-parked issue: no marker yet writes one `someday_recheck_days` days out (`someday_recheck_action: "first-park"`); a still-future marker changes nothing (`"not-due"`); an elapsed marker triggers a CHEAP, zero-scope-agent-cost comparison of the issue's `updatedAt` against the date the marker was written — unchanged since then just refreshes the marker for another cadence window (`"cheap-reset"`, the default, expected-common outcome), while a change (a body edit, a new comment, a label — anything that bumps `updatedAt`) escalates the issue back into `raw_backlog` for exactly ONE real scope-agent pass this session (`"escalate"`) rather than reopening it to ordinary dispatch eligibility forever. Set `0` to disable the cadence entirely and restore #1406's original behavior — a Someday-parked issue is never reconsidered until a human moves it out of the milestone by hand. See `commands/do-work-RATIONALE.md`'s Someday-milestone recheck-cadence writeup for why this reuses `do-work-blocked-until`'s marker SHAPE (not its exact marker name) rather than the `scope.diagnosis_reuse_hours` freshness window or a fourth cadence mechanism.

triage.description: Controls the investigate-then-fix worker mode for untriaged / Sentry-authored issues (issue #514). When the orchestrator dispatches `mode: investigate` against an untriaged issue, the worker investigates the crash, rewrites the body into a real spec, and dispositions into fix / needs-human-review / auto-close. These knobs cap the worker's auto-close authority and the per-session investigation budget. Phase 1 (#514) ships the static spec + routing + config surface; the orchestrator-side dispatch decision (which untriaged issues route to investigate-mode) is a deferred follow-up.

auto_close.description: How much auto-close authority the investigate worker has for the not-actionable disposition. 'confident-only' (default) = close only certain noise (retry/backoff proven in-code, release rolled back) or exact-fingerprint duplicates; otherwise route to needs-human-review. 'off' = NEVER auto-close — always route non-actionable issues to needs-human-review for a person to close. 'aggressive' = also close low-confidence noise and near-duplicates (same root cause, different fingerprint).

max_investigations_per_session.description: Soft cap on investigate-mode dispatches per /do-work session. Investigation burns more tokens with lower merge yield than spec'd issue-work (a crash may disposition to needs-human-review or auto-close with no PR), so this caps the cost exposure. When null (default), no cap. When set, the orchestrator dispatches investigate-mode against at most this many untriaged issues per session and surfaces the rest in the end-of-session summary.

default.description: Default size of the /do-work rolling worker pool when no --concurrency CLI flag is passed. Defaults to 1 (sequential) — most repos bump a manifest (plugin.json) or version row (CHANGELOG.md) on every PR, which the dispatch rules treat as a HARD path collision, parking every second-slot candidate. Set to 2 or higher only on repos where most PRs don't claim a shared manifest/version path and realized parallelism is real. See issue #268 for the dogfooding rationale.

soft_collision_paths.description: Per-repo extension of the built-in soft-collision glob set. The orchestrator unions this array with the built-in default set (defined in commands/do-work/steady-state.md's Dispatch rules) AND any --soft-collision-path CLI flags at dispatch time. Arrays here are additive, not replacing — the layered merge of config (last-wins) still applies, but the *consumer* (orchestrator) does the three-way union. Globs follow bash globstar semantics: `**` matches across path segments, `*` matches within a segment. See issue #254 for the dogfooding rationale (shipyard's own do-work spec files force effective concurrency=1 without this extension).

main_ci.description: Controls which workflows on the default branch make main 'red' for purposes of enqueueing a fix-main-ci divert (step 4.5a). See issue #262 — by default, only branch-protection-required workflows gate; non-required infra/release helpers still surface in the status line as informational but never trigger a divert.

aggregation_mode.description: How to scope the gating set. 'branch-protection' (default) reads required_status_checks from the default branch's protection rule and gates on those workflows only. 'all-workflows' restores pre-#262 behavior — every workflow gates, no branch-protection probe. Setting `required_workflows` to a non-empty array overrides this and acts as an explicit list.

required_workflows.description: Explicit list of workflow names that gate main_ci.status red. Highest priority — when non-empty, overrides `aggregation_mode` and the branch-protection probe. Match is case-sensitive against `workflowName` from `gh run list`. Empty array (the default) defers to `aggregation_mode`.

max_fix_attempts.description: Attempt cap for the fix-main-ci divert per failing-workflow signature within a session (issue #589). After this many consecutive fix-main-ci PRs that each went green on their own PR run but left main's merge-commit red on the SAME workflow, the orchestrator stops auto-dispatching the divert and surfaces a structured flake escalation (recommend quarantine + tracking issue, or human CI-side investigation) instead of burning another CI suite. The fix-main-ci analogue of the blocked:ci 3-attempt cap for fix-checks. Default 3.

merge_gate.description: Local-only-CI merge gate (issue #643). On a repo where the merge-blocking commit status is posted by a MANUALLY-run command rather than by cloud CI that auto-runs on push (e.g. lightwork's `local-ci` status, posted only after a session runs `npm run ci:report` — a ~20 min emulator-backed suite), `--auto` is armed but never fires because nothing posts the gate status. When `command` is set, the orchestrator runs it against each shipped PR's HEAD after the `shipped`/`green` reconcile so the status lands and `--auto` can merge. Defaults preserve cloud-CI behavior unchanged (empty `command` = no gate runs). See do-work/drain.md → 'Local-only-CI merge gate' for the run loop and the single-shared-resource pacing pattern.

command.description: Shell command run against each shipped PR's HEAD (checked-out worktree) to post the local merge-gate commit status. Empty string (the default) means cloud-CI behavior is unchanged — the orchestrator never runs a gate command and relies on checks completing automatically on push, exactly as before #643. Example: `npm run ci:report`. The command runs in a checked-out worktree on the PR's head commit; it is expected to post the gate commit-status for that SHA (success or failure) as a side effect. A non-empty value engages the merge-gate loop in drain.md.

serialize.description: When true, the orchestrator runs at most ONE `command` invocation at a time across the whole session — required when the gate command contends on a single shared machine-wide resource (an emulator with a fixed port, a serialization lock, a single test database). Concurrent gate runs on such a resource fail on contention (port-in-use, lock-held) rather than on code, producing false failures. With `serialize: true` the orchestrator waits for the in-flight gate run to finish (and reaps any orphaned resource — see drain.md's wait-for-free + orphan-reap pattern) before starting the next. Default false (the gate command is safe to run in parallel — stateless or per-worktree-isolated).

max_unmerged_ahead.description: Pacing cap: the maximum number of shipped-but-unmerged PRs the orchestrator lets accumulate ahead of the merge gate before it pauses opening new gate runs to let the gate catch up. Because each `command` run is expensive (the #643 repro was ~20 min/run), the orchestrator does NOT fire a gate run for every shipped PR immediately; it keeps at most this many PRs queued ahead of the gate. Lower it (e.g. 1) on a very slow / heavily-contended gate to minimize concurrent pressure; raise it when the gate is cheaper and you want more throughput. Default 2 (matches the #643 operator's manual choice of 'keep ≤2 unmerged PRs ahead of the gate').

clear_state_command.description: Optional cleanup command run in the gate-runner worktree BEFORE each `command` invocation, to clear stale generated state that a REUSED worktree carries between gate runs (issue #643). The #643 session hit stale gitignored Expo typed-routes in a reused `ci:report` runner, which produced a spurious gate failure. When set, the orchestrator runs this command (e.g. `git clean -fdX -- app` or a project-specific reset) to evict generated/gitignored artifacts so each gate run starts from a clean generated state. Empty string (default) means no pre-run cleanup — appropriate when the gate command regenerates its own state or runs in a fresh worktree per run. Leave empty unless a reused gate-runner worktree demonstrably carries stale generated files between runs.

version_coordination.description: Coordinate the next-available manifest version across in-flight `session_prs` so multiple workers don't all bump to the same row (issue #339). When `enabled: true`, the orchestrator's step C issue-work dispatch scans `session_prs` for PRs that already bumped `manifest_path` and injects `next_available_version` into the worker's dispatch prompt — the worker MUST honor it rather than computing one from `origin/main` HEAD. Defaults preserve pre-#339 behavior (no coordination); flip `enabled: true` on repos where every PR bumps a shared manifest row (the shipyard plugin itself is the canonical case).

enabled.description: When true, engage the orchestrator-side next-available-version computation. When false (default), the dispatch prompt omits the `next_available_version` field and workers bump from `origin/main` HEAD as before.

manifest_path.description: Path (relative to repo root) of the manifest file whose version row is coordination-managed. Example for the shipyard plugin: `plugins/shipyard/.claude-plugin/plugin.json`. Empty string disables coordination even when `enabled: true`.

manifest_version_jq.description: jq expression that extracts the version string from `manifest_path`. Defaults to `.version` (covers `package.json` / `plugin.json` / most JSON manifests).

changelog_path.description: Optional path (relative to repo root) of the CHANGELOG file whose `### <version>` heading row is coordination-managed alongside the manifest. Surfaced in the dispatch prompt so the worker knows to add a fresh entry above the highest in-flight version. Empty string means the worker only honors `next_available_version` for the manifest and is free to compose changelog prose without coordination.

serialize_drain_rebase.description: When true (default) AND `enabled` is true AND `changelog_path` is non-empty, the end-of-session drain phase caps effective fix-rebase concurrency to 1 — it dispatches a fix-rebase for at most one DIRTY PR per poll and waits for it to merge (or settle) before rebasing the next. Closes issue #438: on repos where every PR appends a top-of-file CHANGELOG entry, parallel drain rebases cannot converge — each merge moves the CHANGELOG insert point, re-DIRTYing every sibling that just rebased, so the only stable order is one-at-a-time. The cap applies ONLY to fix-rebase dispatch; fix-checks-only dispatch against red PRs is unaffected (a red PR is urgent regardless of the CHANGELOG serialization point). Set false to restore parallel drain rebases on a coordinated repo whose CHANGELOG convention is conflict-free (e.g. per-PR fragment files merged at release time).

append_only_paths.description: Paths (relative to repo root) of append-only docs whose fix-rebase conflicts are resolved deterministically, independent of `enabled` (issue #1309). fix-rebase.md §4.6 recognizes each listed path the same way it recognizes `manifest_path`/`changelog_path` — a conflicted file set consisting ONLY of these paths (plus, when coordination is also enabled, the manifest/changelog rows) resolves instead of bailing. Per-file resolution: regenerate the conflict in diff3 style and, IF every hunk's common-ancestor section is empty (neither side touched pre-existing shared content — both sides purely appended), concatenate both sides and drop the markers; if any hunk's ancestor section is non-empty (a real shared-content edit), bail unchanged. Default `[]` (no paths recognized — the pre-#1309 all-or-nothing behavior is unchanged until a repo opts a path in). This repo's own value is `["plugins/shipyard/commands/do-work-RATIONALE.md"]` — the documented convention for recording a decision, so its conflicts are almost always two independently-appended sections.

path.description: Path (relative to repo root) of a generated/derived file whose content is a pure function of the tree — a content-hash manifest, a lockfile, a generated type or directory module.

command.description: The exact command (run from repo root inside the rebased worktree) that regenerates `path` from current source. Must be deterministic and side-effect-free beyond writing `path`.

generated_paths.description: Config-declared generated files whose fix-rebase conflicts are resolved by RE-RUNNING the declared `command`, never by hand-merging (issue #1445). fix-rebase.md step 4's lockfile-and-generated-files bullet recognizes each listed `path` the same way the four canonical lockfiles are already recognized; when the regeneration succeeds, the worker records a whole-file exemption in the known-rewrites file so step 5.8's line-survival guard doesn't misread the fresh regenerated content as corruption of the PR's originally-committed content. Deliberately an explicit per-path allowlist, not a glob or a filename heuristic — a repo maintainer opts a path in and states exactly how to regenerate it, so a file the worker merely hand-edits (rather than regenerates) is never silently exempted just because its name looks generated. Default `[]` (no paths recognized — pre-#1445 behavior unchanged until a repo opts a path in). Independent of `enabled`, mirroring `append_only_paths`.

ci.description: CI-minute discipline knobs (issue #323) plus drain-duration knobs (issue #374). The #323 keys default to pre-#323 behavior — they must be set non-default to engage the cost-saving paths. The #374 keys (`settled_minutes`, `max_drain_hours`) ship with active non-zero defaults (20 min / 8 h) because they replace the old hardcoded drain ceiling rather than gating an opt-in path. The end-of-session summary surfaces a `CI cost:` block whenever any #323 key is non-default so the operator sees what got skipped.

skip_drain_rebase.description: When true, the end-of-session drain phase skips ALL fix-rebase dispatch. DIRTY PRs surface in the end-of-session summary as 'needs manual rebase' instead of consuming one full CI suite per force-push. Right default for cost-conscious operators on repos with expensive E2E / Lighthouse suites. Mutually compatible with `max_drain_rebases` — when both are set, `skip_drain_rebase: true` wins (no rebases at all).

max_drain_rebases.description: Soft cap on drain-phase fix-rebase dispatches per session. When null (default), no cap — every DIRTY PR gets a rebase. When set, dispatch fix-rebase on the top-N DIRTY PRs (lowest PR number first, matching drain.md's deterministic ordering) and surface the rest in the summary. Compromise between full-sweep and `skip_drain_rebase: true`.

verify_check_failing_on_head_before_disp.description: When true, before dispatching `fix-checks-only` against a PR in `failed_prs`, the orchestrator's step C pops the entry and verifies the failing check's run-SHA matches the PR's current `headRefOid`. If the failing run is stale (the head has advanced past it — a fresh push superseded the failure already), drop the entry without dispatch and log the skip. Closes the false-failure-re-dispatch path that triggers a redundant full CI suite. Defaults to false (preserves pre-#323 behavior) — flip to true on repos with expensive CI.

skip_speculative_rerun.description: When true, the orchestrator never invokes `gh run rerun` speculatively to clear stale-failure rollups. Defaults to true because the spec doesn't formally cover orchestrator-issued reruns today; this key codifies the absence so a future change that wants to add speculative reruns has to flip it explicitly. A typical push event re-triggers checks naturally via `pull_request` / `push`; explicit rerun adds runner-minutes without changing the outcome.

require_in_progress_check_to_settle.description: When true, if a `failed_prs` candidate has any check with status IN_PROGRESS / PENDING / QUEUED on the latest SHA, defer the dispatch until the run settles (the next step-D refresh re-evaluates). Prevents the double-push case where the orchestrator dispatches fix-checks against an in-progress run, the worker pushes a fix, and now TWO full CI suites are running on overlapping SHAs. Defaults to false (preserves pre-#323 behavior). Independent of `verify_check_failing_on_head_before_dispatch` — they target different races (this one: in-progress checks; that one: stale failed checks).

settled_minutes.description: End-of-session drain: how many minutes a pending session_pr's `headRefOid` must stay unchanged before the PR counts as 'settled' (issue #374). Replaces the old global 5-poll (5-min) no-forward-progress window with a per-PR head-movement threshold. A PR whose head commit hasn't moved for `settled_minutes` is treated as settled even if its checks are still PENDING/IN_PROGRESS — auto-merge is waiting on long-running checks, not stuck. Drain exits when ALL session_prs are settled (merged/closed, `blocked:ci`, rebase-blocked, rate-limit-capped, or pending-with-head-unchanged-for-settled_minutes). Raise it for repos with very long CI (multi-shard E2E + Lighthouse) so a slow-but-healthy merge train isn't called settled prematurely; the default 20 accommodates a typical 3-shard E2E + Lighthouse cycle.

max_drain_hours.description: End-of-session drain: the ultimate wall-clock ceiling, in hours, after which drain forcibly exits even if forward progress is still observable (issue #374). Replaces the old hardcoded 120-min (2-hour) ceiling that fired on wall-clock time rather than progress signal — a healthy multi-PR merge train with full E2E sharding + release-please cascades can legitimately exceed 2 hours. The progress-based `settled_minutes` exit is the primary termination path; this is the belt-and-braces safety net so a degenerate session (runaway CI loop, infinite rebase) still can't run forever. Default 8h; lower it on cheap-CI repos where a >1h drain is itself a smell.

backpressure_multiplier.description: Dispatch-time queue-depth backpressure threshold (issue #1156), only meaningful when `.ci_capacity.shape == "self-hosted"` (issue #1141's one-time session-start pool-shape read). Before filling a freed dispatch slot, `/shipyard:do-work` steady-state.md step C re-reads the LIVE queued-run count and holds the slot (mirroring the existing 'leave the slot empty for now' path used for path/lockfile collisions) when queued runs exceed `pool_total × backpressure_multiplier`. Deliberately looser than the end-of-session summary's fixed 3× *advisory* threshold ([#1141](https://github.com/mattsears18/shipyard/issues/1141)) — a dispatch-blocking hold has a real cost (an idle worker slot) that a passive summary line doesn't, so the default is set higher. Lower it to make the session more conservative about piling CI runs onto a saturated pool; raise it (or set very high) to make backpressure effectively advisory-only.

backpressure_min_in_flight.description: Escape valve for the `backpressure_multiplier` dispatch-time hold (issue #1156): backpressure never fires while fewer than this many workers are already in flight, so a saturated self-hosted CI pool can never fully stall the session with backlog work still waiting and every slot held empty. Default 1 guarantees at least one worker always stays dispatched. Set to 0 to disable the escape valve (backpressure can hold every slot, including the last one, on a sufficiently deep queue) — not recommended outside debugging, since it can produce a session that goes fully idle despite non-empty queues.

prefer_cheap_under_backpressure.description: When a dispatch-time backpressure hold (`backpressure_multiplier`, above) would otherwise leave a freed slot empty (issue #1157, follow-up to #1141/#1156), bias candidate selection toward an issue whose changed-file footprint is likely to skip the repo's heavy CI path instead of just holding the slot. Only ever engages when BOTH conditions hold: a hold verdict actually fired this turn, AND the repo's `pull_request`-triggered workflows declare a `paths-ignore:` cheap path (`scripts/detect-ci-cheap-path.sh`'s repo-shape read, cached once at session start in `.ci_capacity.cheap_ci_globs`) — a repo with no such path is a no-op regardless of this setting, since there is no cheap lane to bias toward. This is a pool-FILTER at the moment of a hold, never a ranking override: normal severity/priority ordering (P0/P1/P2, label priority) is unchanged, and outside a backpressure hold this knob has zero effect. Set false to restore #1156's unconditional-hold behavior (always park the slot under backpressure, regardless of candidate CI cost).

awaiting_external.description: Bounds the orchestrator-owned `awaiting_external` park queue (issue #1390). A worker whose task genuinely cannot finish until a long external job it already started — a dispatched CI run, an EAS/store build, a deploy — reaches a terminal state returns the terminal `awaiting-external` outcome instead of spinning on a narrative non-terminal return; the orchestrator holds the entry, re-runs the worker-supplied probe once per periodic-refresh tick, and resumes the SAME agent when it goes terminal. These knobs bound that wait so a wedged runner pool cannot strand a session.

enabled.description: Whether the orchestrator accepts an `awaiting-external` park at all. When false, an `awaiting-external` return is immediately degraded to a `blocked:` hand-back naming the unfinished job (routed to `needs-human-review` like any other refuse) and no queue entry is created — the pre-#1390 behavior, minus the narrative spin. Turn it off on a repo where every external job is fast enough that a park is never worth the slot bookkeeping, or to isolate the feature while debugging.

max_hours.description: Wall-clock ceiling, in hours, on how long a single `awaiting_external` entry may stay parked before the orchestrator degrades it to a genuine `blocked:` hand-back naming the still-unfinished job. Anchored at the entry's FIRST park and never extended by a re-park, so a worker cannot roll the window forward indefinitely by parking again on each resume. A worker's own `awaiting_eta` is advisory and never overrides this. Default 2h — comfortably above the ~40-minute self-hosted mobile-E2E run that motivated #1390, while still well inside a session. Raise it on repos whose store/deploy pipelines legitimately run for hours; lower it where a >30-minute external wait is itself a smell worth surfacing to a human.

paused_on_environment.description: Bounds the session-wide `paused_on_environment` pause (issue #1402) — distinct from `awaiting_external`, which parks ONE worker on a job it started. This pauses the WHOLE dispatch loop instead of ending the session when a transient, self-clearing environmental condition (currently: self-hosted CI queue-depth backpressure, issues #1156/#1399) would otherwise leave the loop with no future notification to wake it. A bounded `Monitor` watch (`scripts/watch-resume-probe.sh`) re-checks the condition and resumes the loop automatically instead of requiring a human to notice the condition cleared and re-invoke `/do-work`.

enabled.description: Whether the orchestrator may enter a `paused_on_environment` pause at all. When false, the deadlock condition that would otherwise trigger a pause instead falls through to the pre-#1402 behavior (the turn ends with a `parked (...)` idle_reason and no resume mechanism is armed) — turn off to isolate the feature while debugging, or on a repo where the underlying deadlock condition (backpressure holding at `ci.backpressure_min_in_flight: 0`) is never configured.

max_hours.description: Wall-clock ceiling, in hours, on how long a single pause may stay active before the orchestrator degrades it to a genuine hand-back naming the still-saturated environment. Anchored at the pause's FIRST activation and never extended by a re-pause, mirroring `awaiting_external.max_hours`'s anchoring rule exactly — a session cannot roll the window forward indefinitely by re-pausing on the same condition. Default 4h — double `awaiting_external`'s default, since a saturated CI pool clearing (the #1402 repro observed real recovery in 45 minutes) is a coarser, less time-critical signal than a single dispatched job's ETA; lower it on a repo where a multi-hour environmental stall is itself worth surfacing to a human sooner.

poll_interval_seconds.description: How often `scripts/watch-resume-probe.sh` re-checks the environmental condition while paused. Default 5 minutes — deliberately coarser than step C's own live per-dispatch re-read, since a genuinely self-clearing condition resolves on the order of tens of minutes (the #1402 repro: 45 idle minutes), and a tighter interval only spends extra `gh` API calls with no added value.

pause_when_in_flight_at_or_below.description: The `in_flight` worker count (after this turn's dispatch decisions) at or below which a backpressure hold transitions into a session-wide pause instead of just leaving the slot empty for the next completion to retry. Default `0` — pause ONLY at the genuine dead-end (no worker remains in flight, so no future completion notification will ever re-trigger a retry). Under the default `ci.backpressure_min_in_flight: 1` escape valve, a hold verdict guarantees `in_flight >= 1`, so this condition is unreachable in the common case; it exists specifically to rescue a session where an operator has set `ci.backpressure_min_in_flight: 0` (already documented there as producing 'a session that goes fully idle despite non-empty queues') from a silent full stall. Raise it (e.g. to `1`) to pause proactively whenever the loop would otherwise be grinding at minimum concurrency into a saturated pool, rather than only at the strict zero-in-flight case — more aggressive, and a legitimate choice on a repo where even one worker's worth of CI-minute spend under sustained backpressure isn't worth it.

scope.description: Controls scope-preflight caching, pre-scope detector behavior, and worker scope discipline (issues #563, #591, #1623). The freshness window lets the orchestrator skip redundant scope-agent dispatches when a matching marker-tagged diagnosis comment already exists on the issue and is younger than `diagnosis_reuse_hours`. The self-modification path set drives the Detector 2 pre-defer for issues whose deliverable is an Auto-Mode-denied Claude-Code agent-config file.

inline_incidental_fixes.description: Whether an issue-work worker may fix an incidental problem it finds in the SAME PR instead of filing a follow-up issue (issue #1623). Default true. The original rule mandated filing on the grounds that scope creep 'makes PRs unreviewable and stalls auto-merge'. The reviewability half assumes a human reads the diff, which is false for a repo whose worker PRs land via auto-merge with no reviewer — while the cost is paid on every dispatch: a new issue per incidental finding, plus a second full worker dispatch to apply a fix the first worker had already diagnosed with the file open. The auto-merge half survives, and is preserved as a BOUND rather than a prohibition: a worker still files instead of fixing when the fix reaches an unrelated subsystem, needs a design decision the dispatched issue cannot settle, or is large enough to meaningfully raise the chance of reddening a required check. Set to false to restore the always-file behavior — appropriate for a repo where worker PRs ARE human-reviewed and diff size carries real review cost.
inline_incidental_fixes._comment: Does NOT relax the separate 'no drive-by refactors, no unrelated cleanups' rule in issue-work.md step 4, which is about design restraint rather than incidental-finding disposition, nor the phase_1_scope slice boundary the orchestrator supplies at dispatch time.

diagnosis_reuse_hours.description: How many hours a marker-tagged scope-preflight diagnosis comment is considered fresh enough to reuse without re-dispatching a scope agent. When the newest such comment on an issue is younger than this window AND its mechanical evidence still re-validates cheaply (cited blockers still open, body unchanged), the orchestrator records the defer with provenance 'cached-diagnosis' instead of dispatching a new scope agent. Set to 0 to disable caching entirely (always re-dispatch). Default 72h.

self_modification_paths.description: Path fragments that Detector 2 (setup.md step 6 pre-scope detector batch, issue #591) treats as Claude-Code self-modification targets. When an issue's DELIVERABLE is editing one of these paths, the Claude Code auto-mode classifier applies a HARD BLOCK not cleared by user intent, so a worker dispatch can never ship the change — the orchestrator synthesizes a `human-decision-required` defer instead of burning a ~100k-token worker dispatch. Trailing-slash entries (e.g. `.claude/hooks/`) match any path under that directory. Set to an EMPTY array (`[]`) to disable Detector 2 entirely — appropriate for users NOT running under Auto Mode, where edits to these paths succeed normally and the pre-defer would be a false positive that strands shippable work in the human-review queue. Default covers the four known Auto-Mode-denied agent-config surfaces.

orchestrator_only_skills.description: Skill/command name tokens that Detector 3 (setup.md step 6 pre-scope detector batch, issue #1294) treats as orchestrator-only — a dispatched `/shipyard:do-work` worker is spec-prohibited from ever invoking them (see `skills/worker-preamble/milestone-prohibition.md` and each named skill's own 'Who runs this'/frontmatter boundary). When an issue's DELIVERABLE explicitly instructs a worker to invoke one of these tokens, the orchestrator synthesizes a `human-decision-required` defer instead of burning a worker dispatch that can only discover the prohibition and bail. Matched as a case-insensitive substring against the issue body in a deliverable context (a suggested-fix/acceptance-criteria framing), ignoring a leading `/` slash-command prefix. Set to an EMPTY array (`[]`) to disable Detector 3 entirely. Default covers the one known orchestrator-only skill, `shipyard:update-roadmap`.

co_scope_keys.description: Body-marker keys that make issues co-scope candidates for scope pre-flight (issue #1596, commands/do-work/setup/06h-co-scope-grouping.md). Eligible issues whose bodies carry the same `<!-- <key>=<value> -->` marker (by default `audit-run`, which every /shipyard:audit filing stamps) are scoped by ONE scope agent over the whole set, which returns a `separate` / `one-pr` / `partial` grouping verdict alongside the unchanged per-issue entries — so two sibling findings that are one change (e.g. two bugs that both need the same version-constant bump) ship as one PR instead of two PRs conflicting on the same line. The default verdict is `separate`; a bundle stands only when scripts/co-scope-groups.sh validate confirms a shared file in every bundled issue's scoped `files`. Keys must match [a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]*. Set to an EMPTY array (`[]`) to disable co-scoping and scope every candidate individually.

external_dependency_recheck_days.description: How many days out an `external-dependency` scope-preflight defer's self-clearing `<!-- do-work-blocked-until: YYYY-MM-DD -->` recheck marker is set from today (issue #1195). Written into the issue body in addition to the `agent-console` label so the proactive operator sweep can skip re-enqueueing (and re-judging) the issue while the date is still future, instead of re-litigating an unchanged upstream condition every tick. Computed entirely orchestrator-side from today's UTC date — never derived from scope-agent-supplied text, so every external-dependency defer gets a marker regardless of what the agent wrote in `evidence_pointer`. Does not affect dispatch eligibility (the `agent-console` label already excludes the issue from `raw_backlog`).

recheck_probe_enabled.description: Whether the proactive operator sweep evaluates a `<!-- do-work-recheck: <verb> <args...> -->` companion body marker (issue #1198, scripts/eval-recheck-probe.sh) before falling back to the plain `do-work-blocked-until` calendar check on an `agent-console`-labeled issue. Set to `false` to disable probe evaluation entirely and always fall through to the calendar-only check — the pre-#1198 behavior. Does not affect whether a `do-work-blocked-until` marker itself is honored; it only gates whether a companion recorded-probe marker gets evaluated.

recheck_probe_timeout_seconds.description: Bounded timeout, in seconds, for a single `do-work-recheck` probe command (`npm view` / `gh api` / `curl`) run by scripts/eval-recheck-probe.sh. A probe that exceeds this timeout is treated as `unknown` and falls through to the plain `do-work-blocked-until` calendar check — never treated as evidence the blocking condition changed.

recheck_probe_url_hosts.description: Per-repo allowlist of host names the `url-json` `do-work-recheck` probe verb (issue #1496) may contact. EMPTY BY DEFAULT, which makes the verb inert: on a repo that has not opted in, every `url-json` marker resolves to `unknown` and no outbound request is ever made. This is the security boundary for the verb — the marker itself lives in an issue body (untrusted, editable by any collaborator after the author-trust check ran), whereas this list lives in the repo's COMMITTED `shipyard.config.json` and can only change through a reviewed PR. So an issue-body edit can pick a URL only among hosts a human already approved. Exact host match, case-insensitive, NO wildcards and no implicit subdomain matching — list `reviews.example.com` explicitly rather than expecting `example.com` to cover it. Hosts are matched against a URL that already had to be HTTPS, port-less, credential-less, and named by a DNS name rather than an IP literal (see scripts/eval-recheck-probe.sh's header for the full grammar).

recheck_probe_max_bytes.description: Response-size cap, in bytes, for the `url-json` `do-work-recheck` probe verb (issue #1496). Enforced twice: passed to curl as `--max-filesize` (which only fires when the server declares a Content-Length) and re-checked in-script against the actually-received body (which holds for a chunked or streamed response too). A response over the cap is treated as `unknown` — never as evidence the blocking condition changed. Does not apply to the `npm-view` / `gh-api` verbs, whose outputs are already single scalars.

decompose.description: Controls inline auto-decomposition of confirmed epics inside /do-work (issue #665). When a scope-preflight defer is `confirmed-non-shippable-as-single-PR` with a mechanically-decomposable `evidence_pointer` prefix (`Multi-PR sequence:` or `Missing dependency:`), the orchestrator inline-invokes the `/decompose-epic` worker logic (the single source of truth for the sharding) to shard the epic into an ordered `Blocked by #<sibling>` sub-issue chain right then — no human round-trip. The confidence gate + `max_subissues` cap are the guardrails: a low-confidence or over-cap breakdown, and every non-mechanical evidence class, still falls through to the human handoff (`needs-human-review` + trigger marker preserved).

auto.description: When true (default), /do-work inline auto-decomposes `confirmed-non-shippable-as-single-PR` epics whose `evidence_pointer` prefix is `Multi-PR sequence:` or `Missing dependency:` — reusing the `/decompose-epic` worker logic — instead of parking them for a manual `/decompose-epic` invocation. Set to false to restore the pre-#665 defer-to-human behavior: the epic gets `needs-human-review` + the `<!-- do-work-needs-decomposition -->` trigger marker and waits for an explicit `/decompose-epic` run. Non-mechanical evidence classes (`Multi-service coordination:`, `Body cites <artifact>:`) always defer to the human handoff regardless of this flag.

max_subissues.description: Hard cap on the number of sub-issues the inline auto-decompose path (and the standalone `/decompose-epic --max-subissues`) will create per epic. A confident breakdown that would exceed the cap escalates to the human handoff rather than fanning out — an epic that won't shard cleanly under the cap is too big to decompose mechanically. Default 8.

dependencies.description: Controls how a /shipyard:do-work worker chooses the version when its implementation INTRODUCES a new dependency (issue #694). Applies at dependency introduction only — never to upgrading existing deps (that's Dependabot / a separate audit dimension). The peer/SDK carve-out (a framework-constrained package — React / React Native, @react-native-firebase/*, expo-* — must use the framework-required version) is UNCONDITIONAL and is not disabled by any value here, because an SDK-mismatched version is a correctness bug, not a policy preference.

new_dep_version.description: Version-selection policy when a worker adds a NEW dependency. `latest-stable` (default): install the current latest stable version (`npm install <pkg>@latest` or the ecosystem equivalent) and record the resolved version in the PR body, so a newly-added dep starts current rather than accruing introduction-time version debt. `conservative`: pin new introductions to a documented older baseline — appropriate for a repo deliberately trailing the ecosystem. The peer/SDK carve-out overrides BOTH values for framework-constrained packages.

worktree_reap.description: Controls the setup step-3b cross-session sweep of stale `agent-*` worktrees (issue #836) and the mid-session disk-space backpressure guard (issue #1261). The sweep reaps at most `max_per_session` reap-eligible worktrees per session, oldest-first, via `worktree-reap.sh reap-stale` — the on-disk backlog itself is the checkpoint, so a session that can't clear the whole backlog still makes forward progress and a later session continues from where it left off. `warn_threshold` gates a one-time session-start advisory when the `agent-*` count is high enough that the backlog is worth a human's attention regardless of the per-session cap. `disk_free_floor_mb` gates the same `reap-stale` sweep running mid-session, before a dispatch, whenever free disk space drops below the floor.

max_per_session.description: Maximum number of stale `agent-*` worktrees the step-3b sweep will actually remove in a single session, oldest-first by worktree-directory mtime. Peer-alive worktrees (a live, non-self process still holds the lock) are always deferred and do NOT count against this cap. Worktrees beyond the cap are left untouched on disk — never partially removed — so a subsequent session's sweep continues the backlog from where this one stopped. Set to 0 to disable removal entirely (classification/reporting still runs); raise it on a repo with fast local disk and few concurrent CI-relevant worktrees.

warn_threshold.description: When the number of `agent-*` worktrees still on disk at session start meets or exceeds this threshold, the setup step prints a one-time advisory naming the count and the reclaimable disk size, so a backlog large enough to matter (each worktree can carry its own `node_modules/`, easily 1+ GB) is visible even though the per-session reap cap means it won't all clear in one session. Set to 0 to always warn when any `agent-*` worktree exists; set very high to effectively disable the warning.

disk_free_floor_mb.description: Issue #1261 — the mid-session disk-space backpressure floor (megabytes) checked at every steady-state step C dispatch decision via `worktree-reap.sh disk-check` against the volume holding `.claude/worktrees`. When free space drops below this floor, step C runs a bounded `reap-stale` sweep (respecting `.in_flight` exclusion per issue #832, never inferring liveness from branch name per issue #836) BEFORE dispatching a replacement worker — a backstop for whatever gap let the ordinary per-completion reap points (A.0.5 / A.1 / step B / dispatch-rules.md 2d) fall behind, not a replacement for any of them. The reading (post-sweep, if one ran) is surfaced as the invariant line's `disk_free_mb=` token regardless of whether the floor was crossed. Set to 0 to disable the guard (the check still reads and reports free space, but never triggers a sweep).

flake_registry.description: Cross-PR / cross-session flake registry (issue #378). When `enabled: true`, the `fix-checks-only` worker records one event line per flake conclusion into `~/.shipyard/flake-registry.jsonl` (via scripts/flake-registry.sh `record`), and a setup/dispatch-time reader aggregates per-(workflow,job,test) flake rates over the window to surface chronic flakes that should be escalated rather than silently re-run. Defaults preserve pre-#378 behavior (disabled — no recording, no escalation). Phase 1 ships the data layer (record + windowed report + threshold evaluation); the three escalation ACTIONS are evaluated by `flake-registry.sh crossed` but ENFORCEMENT (filing tracking issues, writing flake-suspects, applying blocked:ci) is a deferred follow-up phase.

enabled.description: When true, the `fix-checks-only` worker records flake events to the registry and the orchestrator computes flake rates at setup/dispatch time. When false (default), no recording and no escalation — pre-#378 per-PR-only flake handling.

window_days.description: Rolling window (in days) over which flake events are aggregated when computing per-test flake rates and evaluating the escalation threshold. Events older than the window don't count toward escalation.

rerun_threshold.description: A (workflow, job, test) flake crosses the escalation bar when it has accumulated at least this many flake events within `window_days`. Combined with `distinct_prs_threshold` (both must be met).

distinct_prs_threshold.description: A flake crosses the escalation bar only if its events span at least this many DISTINCT PRs within `window_days`. Guards against a single PR's repeated reruns being misread as a chronic cross-PR flake. Combined with `rerun_threshold` (both must be met).

actions.description: The escalation actions to take when a flake crosses the threshold. `file-tracking-issue` opens a chronic-flake tracking issue; `stop-auto-rerunning` adds the test to a flake-suspects list so fix-checks-only stops auto-rerunning it until a human signs off; `apply-blocked-ci` labels affected PRs blocked:ci with a reference to the tracking issue. Phase 1 (#378) ships the threshold evaluation that emits these on each crossed row; ENFORCEMENT of the actions is a deferred follow-up phase.

prune_window_days.description: Issue #863: rolling retention window (in days) for `~/.shipyard/flake-registry.jsonl` itself, distinct from `window_days` (the escalation-aggregation window). The orchestrator's setup step 5.8 passes this to `flake-enforce.sh enforce --prune-window-days` once per session whenever `flake_registry.enabled` is true, which rewrites the registry to drop events older than the window (via `flake-registry.sh prune`) — this is what bounds the registry's on-disk growth in steady state. 0 disables pruning (keep everything). Has no effect while `flake_registry.enabled` is false — nothing is ever recorded to prune.

operator_denial_registry.description: Cross-session operator-denial ledger (issue #1363). `operator_denials` is a session-local orchestrator-state struct recording every operator-phase action (gh pr close/gh pr merge/a browser mutation) the Claude Code auto-mode permission classifier refused outright; it's surfaced in the end-of-session summary but discarded with the session-state file at cleanup. When `enabled: true`, cleanup-summary.md's step 7.6 appends one line per denial (via scripts/operator-denial-registry.sh `record`) to `~/.shipyard/operator-denials.jsonl` BEFORE the session-state file is retired, so a denial class survives past the session that recorded it and a repeated denial on the same (repo, kind, target) is distinguishable from a one-off via `report`. Defaults preserve pre-#1363 behavior (disabled — nothing persisted beyond the session; the in-session `Operator denied (#746)` summary block is unaffected either way). Off by default because the recorded target can be a specific admin-console URL or field name — more identifying than, say, flake-registry's CI test names — so persistence is an explicit opt-in rather than the flake-registry precedent's own default.

enabled.description: When true, cleanup-summary.md's step 7.6 persists this session's `operator_denials` entries to `~/.shipyard/operator-denials.jsonl` before the session-state file is removed. When false (default), no persistence — denials are still recorded and surfaced within the session's own `Operator denied (#746)` summary block, exactly as before #1363; they just don't outlive the session.

prune_window_days.description: Rolling retention window (in days) for `~/.shipyard/operator-denials.jsonl` itself. Kept longer than flake_registry's 90-day default because this ledger's value is in a slow-forming, cross-session pattern rather than a fast-moving CI signal. 0 disables pruning (keep everything). Has no effect while `operator_denial_registry.enabled` is false — nothing is ever recorded to prune.

audits.description: Recurring-cadence configuration for /shipyard:audit dimensions (issue #975). Neither `testing-auditor` nor `functional-qa-auditor` (nor any other audit dimension) ran on any cadence before this — both were invoke-on-demand only, which means they surface drift only once a maintainer already suspects a problem. `/shipyard:audit-scheduled` reads `schedule` below, checks each entry's last-run timestamp against its cadence via `scripts/audit-schedule.sh`, and dispatches only the dimensions that are actually due — reusing `/shipyard:audit`'s existing dispatch table and the `audit-key` fingerprint dedup already built into `filing-github-issues`, so a scheduled run that finds nothing new produces no issue churn for free. Compose with the existing `/loop` skill for the actual periodic trigger (e.g. `/loop 1h /shipyard:audit-scheduled`) — this block only decides WHEN a dimension is due, not how it gets invoked on a wall-clock schedule.

schedule.description: One entry per audit dimension to run on a recurring cadence. Last-run state persists at ~/.shipyard/audit-schedule-state.json, keyed by (owner/repo, dimension) — NOT committed, so it isn't part of this schema.

dimension.description: Audit dimension. Matches /audit's own type argument one-for-one (see commands/audit.md's Dispatching table) — `all` fans out to every auditor exactly as a bare `/audit all` would.

cadence.description: Minimum time between runs of this dimension, as an integer plus a unit suffix: m=minutes, h=hours, d=days, w=weeks. Example: '7d' = weekly, '24h' = daily. Parsed by scripts/audit-schedule.sh's `cadence-seconds` / `due` subcommands — the single source of truth for the format, not re-derived elsewhere.

url.description: URL to pass to this dimension's auditor(s), for URL-dependent dimensions (lighthouse, web-ux, ux, seo, marketing, pwa, a11y, functional-qa). Omit for codebase-only dimensions (testing, dx, tech-debt, docs, observability, api, data-lifecycle, mobile-ux, security without a live surface, release-readiness).

enabled.description: Set false to keep a schedule entry in config (documenting intent) without actually running it — cheaper than deleting and re-adding. A disabled entry never appears in `audit-schedule.sh due`'s output regardless of its recorded last-run state.

my_turn.description: Controls /shipyard:my-turn's Pass B 'authored by $ME, never dispatched' signal (issue #1078). The predicate requires the issue to carry no `shipyard` session-stamp label AND not be self-assigned to `@me` — the two `/do-work` claims a workable issue on dispatch — before it's surfaced, so a freshly-filed issue that simply hasn't had its turn yet isn't misread as a misconfiguration. This knob only tunes the age conjunct.

stale_undispatched_days.description: Minimum age (in days, by `createdAt`) an issue authored by `$ME` must reach — with no `shipyard` label, no self-assignment to `@me`, and no `needs-human-review` label — before /my-turn's Pass B surfaces it as a P2 housekeeping nudge ('/do-work has never picked this up'). Default 7: an issue younger than this has simply not had its turn in a healthy backlog, not been overlooked. Lower it to get an earlier nudge on a low-volume repo; raise it on a repo with a deep backlog where a week's wait is routine.

max_diagnostic_reads_per_item.description: Per-item investigation ceiling (issue #1073): the maximum number of extra `gh` reads /my-turn may spend, beyond the survey projection, deriving a single item's rendered action — never CI-log reads, run-job drill-downs, or any other root-cause investigation, which are always out of scope regardless of this value. Default 1: at most one extra read (e.g. a single `gh pr view` for a field the list projection omitted). Set to 0 to require the rendered action come from the survey projection alone, falling back to the degraded render (known signal + URL + owning command) for anything more. Raise only as an explicit opt-in to deeper per-item grounding on a repo where that tradeoff is wanted.

disposition_call_detection.description: Disposition-call detection toggle (issue #1074): whether /my-turn's Phase 1 recognizes a needs-human-review issue (or draft PR) whose gated work is already complete or all-but-complete as a batchable disposition call (close as done / keep open / close and split), derived entirely from the already-fetched survey projection (labels, updatedAt, last-3-comments, closingIssuesReferences) with no extra gh round-trip. Default true. Set false to disable the heuristic entirely and fall back to the pre-#1074 behavior (such an issue is treated as a plain needs-human-review item, walked in Phase 3) — e.g. if the completion-assertion phrase matching produces false positives on a repo's comment conventions.

assume_operator_enabled.description: Declared assumption (issue #1093) about whether THIS repo's /shipyard:do-work runs are actually draining `agent-console` items via the browser-operator phase. /my-turn's Human-only queue filter excludes agent-console issues on the premise that /do-work's operator phase drains them — true only when /do-work is NOT run with --no-operate / --hands-off. That flag is per-invocation and not persisted, so /my-turn (a separate command run) cannot observe which way the last /do-work run was actually started; reading /do-work's live session state directly is tracked separately by issue #1080 and is NOT what this knob does. Default true matches /do-work's own operator-inclusive-by-default posture — the common case. Set false for a repo whose maintainer habitually runs /do-work with --no-operate / --hands-off: /my-turn then stops filtering agent-console items to a one-line pointer and instead walks them in the human-only queue directly, since nothing is automatically draining them. This is a declared assumption, not an observed fact, and will occasionally be wrong if the invocation pattern varies run to run — it is the best available approximation until #1080 lands.

milestones.description: Top-level, opt-in roadmap-sequencing surface (issue #1239) — independent of every other config block. A `projects` (GitHub Projects v2) block was designed alongside this and deliberately dropped: a project board mostly restates issue state/labels shipyard already tracks natively, and Projects v2 needs the `project` OAuth scope `gh` doesn't grant by default. Phase AUTHORING is deliberately NOT part of this schema — there is no declarative `phases[]` array; naming phases and writing each one's bet is the dispatching agent's job (#1240-#1244), not config. Numbering contract: a milestone's sequence position is read back from a numeric title prefix `N · Title` (U+00B7 MIDDLE DOT, one space on each side) — the separator is fixed, not configurable, so it can't become a per-repo parsing surface for no benefit. The fallback milestone (`fallback` below) always holds the highest `N` and never completes. Every key below is read by exactly one of the four issues this config unblocks, so the feature degrades cleanly — a repo can take milestone assignment without milestone-ordered dispatch, or vice versa. When this block is absent entirely, or `enabled` is false, behavior is byte-for-byte identical to a repo with no `milestones` block at all: no GitHub Milestones API calls, no milestone reads, nothing in `/do-work`'s dispatch order or issue-filing path changes.

enabled.description: Master opt-in switch. Every other key in this block is inert while false — shipyard runs against plenty of repos with no roadmap at all, and silently creating milestones in someone's repo on first run would be a hostile default. Set true (typically via `/shipyard:init`) to turn milestone-sequenced work on.

fallback.description: Title of the fallback milestone shipyard creates automatically when `enabled` is true and the repo has no phase an issue fits. The fallback never completes and always sorts last (i.e. it is created with the highest `N ·` prefix of any milestone in the repo) — an issue that matches no existing phase goes here immediately rather than sitting unmilestoned.

assign_on_file.description: When true, issue-filing paths (`/shipyard:file-issue`, the `*-auditor` agents) assign a milestone to every newly-filed issue — the fallback when no phase fits, else the phase the filer judges the issue belongs to. Has no effect while `enabled` is false.

prioritize_dispatch.description: When true, `/do-work`'s backlog ranking sorts by milestone sequence (the `N ·` prefix) before falling back to the existing P0 > P1 > P2 > unlabeled + staleness ordering — phase 1's issues dispatch before phase 2's regardless of label priority. Has no effect while `enabled` is false.

sweep_on_loop_end.description: When true, the `/do-work` orchestrator runs an end-of-loop sweep that keeps every open issue carrying a milestone (fallback for anything that fell through) and reports phase completion. Has no effect while `enabled` is false.

$comment: Forbidden field surfaces: anything matching /token|secret|api_key|password|credential/i is rejected at load time by shipyard-config.sh — the committed config must never carry secrets. Personal overrides in .shipyard/config.local.json are gitignored but the same rule applies (helps catch accidental paste into the wrong file).
